vocab.notes: Jaký je? What's he like? (Jak vypadá? = What does he look like?)
A false friend: it doesn't mean "sympathetic" (that's soucitný).

dialogue.setting: Friday lunch. Sarah's friend Kateřina asks about her new job.

lines.speaker: Kateřina
lines.cs: Tak co, jak se ti líbí nová [[práce|práce|nom|subject]]?
lines.en: So, how do you like the new job?

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.cs: Moc. [[Kolegové|kolega|nom.pl|subject]] jsou milí a pomáhají mi s [[češtinou|čeština|ins|with-s]].
lines.en: A lot. My colleagues are nice and they help me with my Czech.

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.cs: Je trochu přísný, ale spravedlivý. A je velmi pracovitý.
lines.en: He's a bit strict, but fair. And he's very hard-working.

lines.speaker: Kateřina
lines.cs: To zní dobře. Můj [[šéf|šéf|nom|subject]] je strašně náročný.
lines.en: That sounds good. My boss is terribly demanding.

spoken.note: strašně (terribly) is a very common everyday intensifier, for good things too: strašně milý.

hints.explain: "Přísný" is strict, "spravedlivý" fair; lazy would be "líný".
"Přísný" is strict (funny is "vtipný"); "spravedlivý" is fair.

exercises.why: "Je trochu přísný, ale spravedlivý." He's a bit strict, but fair.

exercises.listen: Kolegové jsou milí a pomáhají mi s češtinou.
options: Nice, and they help with her Czech
Strict, and they speak only English
Nice, but she rarely sees them
answers: Nice, and they help with her Czech

hints.wrong: Strict, and they speak only English
hints.explain: "Milí" is nice, and "pomáhají mi s češtinou": they help me with Czech.

hints.wrong: Nice, but she rarely sees them
hints.explain: "Pomáhají mi s češtinou" means they help her with Czech.

exercises.why: "Kolegové jsou milí a pomáhají mi s češtinou." My colleagues are nice and help me with my Czech.

exercises.prompt: How do you like the new job?
answers: Jak se ti líbí nová práce[?]
exercises.why: See "Word order and the little words": new information goes last, and jsem, se, si, mi, ho… go second.

hints.wrong: jak ti se líbí nová práce
hints.explain: In a group of little words, se comes before ti: Jak se ti líbí…?

exercises.prompt: What's your boss like? (informal; a male boss)
exercises.why: Jaký je…? asks what someone is like as a person. Jaký agrees with šéf (masculine).

hints.explain: Jak vypadá? asks about appearance. For personality: Jaký je tvůj šéf?
Jak je…? is more like "How is he (doing)?". To ask what he's like: Jaký je tvůj šéf?
váš is the formal/plural "your". Informal: tvůj šéf.

exercises.why: For groups of people with at least one man (masculine animate plural), adjectives end in -í: milí kolegové.

hints.explain: -é is the plural for women and things: milé kolegyně. Kolegové (men, or a mixed group) take -í: milí.
kolegové is plural, so the adjective is plural: milí.
přísný is masculine. šéfová (a female boss) needs přísná.

exercises.why: velmi / moc / hodně + adjective: velmi vtipný.

hints.explain: vtipná is feminine. For "he": vtipný.

exercises.why: trochu = a bit; líný = lazy (masculine, so "he").
See "Word order and the little words": new information goes last, and jsem, se, si, mi, ho… go second.

hints.explain: Mi goes second, not at the end: Kolegové mi pomáhají.

exercises.prompt: My colleagues are nice. (a mixed team)
exercises.why: Masculine animate plural: kolegové, with adjectives in -í (milí). sympatický → sympatičtí.

hints.explain: milý is singular. With kolegové use the plural: milí.
milé is for women or things. For a mixed group (kolegové): milí.
For masculine animate plurals, "my" is moji (or mí): moji kolegové.

exercises.prompt: Say you're sorry to hear that.
exercises.why: To mě mrzí or To je mi líto express sympathy ("I'm sorry to hear that").

hints.explain: Promiň is "sorry" for something you did (excuse me). For sympathy: To mě mrzí.
Promiňte is "excuse me / sorry" for something you did. For sympathy: To mě mrzí.

exercises.question: Which case is "milí"?
exercises.why: After být (jsou), a describing adjective stays in the nominative, agreeing with the subject: kolegové → milí.

exercises.en: My colleagues help me with my Czech.
exercises.why: They do it regularly: the imperfective pomáhat → pomáhají.

hints.explain: Pomůžou is "they will help" once. Regularly: pomáhají.

exercises.en: I don't know how to do it. Will you help me?
exercises.why: Asking for help with this one thing: the perfective pomoct → pomůžeš.

hints.explain: Pomáháš mi? is "are you helping me / do you help me?". Asking for one-off help: Pomůžeš mi?
